goals: mechanistic: quantify sensitivity of ELM sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) to soil texture, holding forcing fixed
validation: check warm-started water-table/storage state against sparse USGS wells; flag tile-drain flux as unvalidated

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM with per-column SSURGO soils is the direct lever for a soil-texture-on-drainage question; QDRAI is a default output.

answerable: soil-texture control on ELM diffuse sub-surface drainage (QDRAI), via per-column SSURGO with fixed forcing
relative ranking / spread of drainage across texture classes as a sensitivity result
warm-started water-table state cross-checked against sparse USGS wells

not_answerable.aspect: validation of agricultural drainage magnitude against tile-drain flow
not_answerable.why: tile-drain flow data are missing in-domain AND ELM's QDRAI is a diffuse drainage parameterization, not engineered tile drainage — the dominant real-world drainage pathway here is not represented
not_answerable.needs: tile-drainage process representation in ELM + tile-drain flow observation ingest

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by soil texture only (elevation deliberately not a stratum)

classes: clay (assumed dominant agricultural classes — confirm from SSURGO)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: One column per resolved dominant SSURGO texture class (~5) spans the driver; light ×2 replication separates soil-driven drainage spread from residual NLDAS forcing-cell variation across the basin. Low 160 m relief and a soil-only question make elevation banding a confounder, so it is excluded.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Place replicates in the agricultural interfluves/uplands where each texture class is areally dominant; avoid riparian corridors so the isolated signal is texture, not proximity to the channel/water table.
sampling_strategy.replication: ×2 per texture class to distinguish soil signal from forcing-cell noise

sampling_plan.reason: high-conductivity end member — expect largest, flashiest sub-surface drainage; anchors the sensitivity range
most areally dominant agricultural class; the basin-representative drainage case
low-conductivity, drainage-limited response; tests suppression of QDRAI
fine end member — minimal diffuse drainage, maximum retention; anchors the low end

validation_design.comparison: co-located — compare warm-started/equilibrated ELM water-table state to wells nearest each stratum; sparse, so treat as a state sanity check, not a dense fit
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on well density in-domain

validation_design.comparison: none — no in-domain data and ELM does not represent tile drainage; recorded as a gap, not validated

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: representative multi-year NLDAS forcing window, Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start, native SSURGO soil per column

requires_capabilities.why: drainage/storage are slow states; cold-start default 8.8 m water table would make QDRAI an initialization artifact
requires_capabilities.blocks: meaningful, comparable drainage across texture classes

requires_capabilities.why: needed to resolve and assign dominant texture classes per column
constrain sampling to the Upper Iowa basin
engineered tile drains dominate real agricultural drainage but are absent from ELM's QDRAI
requires_capabilities.blocks: answering the question as an agricultural (tile) drainage question rather than a diffuse-drainage sensitivity

requires_capabilities.why: no in-domain drainage flux data exist
requires_capabilities.blocks: direct validation of the drainage flux

assumptions: SSURGO resolves ~5 dominant agricultural texture classes in-domain (silt loam assumed most extensive) — confirm from raster.
160 m relief produces negligible NLDAS forcing contrast relative to the soil signal, justifying uniform-forcing treatment.
Question intends the ELM diffuse sub-surface drainage term (QDRAI); if the user means engineered tile-drain export, the design is infeasible without new process representation.
A single representative multi-year forcing window (within 1980-2018) is adequate to expose steady-state texture sensitivity.
open_questions: Does 'sub-surface drainage' mean ELM's diffuse QDRAI, or engineered agricultural tile-drain flow? This changes feasibility from partial to infeasible.
How many USGS wells actually fall inside the HUC8, and at what depths?
Preferred forcing window / whether interannual variability (multiple windows) is of interest?
